This is indicative of command and scripting interpreter (T1056.001) and command execution (T1059) techniques. The script also performs file and directory discovery (T1133) and network service discovery (T1105). The user executing these commands is root, which is unusual for normal system activity.

The logs also show the execution of xargs, which is often used to build and execute commands from standard input. This can be used for command and scripting interpreter (T1056.001) and command execution (T1059) as well. The use of xargs in this context, combined with the base64-encoded command, suggests that the attacker is attempting to obfuscate their actions.

The attacker is also accessing objects (T1055) on the system, which could indicate data exfiltration or further system manipulation. The attacker is also using scheduled tasks (T1085) to maintain persistence on the system.

Overall, the logs indicate a high likelihood of an attack, as they show an attacker executing commands, downloading and running a shell script, performing file and network discovery, and scheduling tasks on the system.
